messages.access-read-current-native-toolkit-acces: Read current native toolkit access and routing; performs no toolkit operation.
messages.activity-also-merge-the-events-of-source: Also merge the events of sources this record is directly linked to. Default true.
messages.activity-one-record-s-activity-newest-fi: One record's activity, newest first: its own discussion, recorded emails/messages/developments and CRM membership changes, plus the events of Tasks, Signoffs, Actions and documents it is directly and explicitly linked to (each read with your current access; unreadable sources are omitted). Reading never acknowledges, sends or changes anything. Page with next_cursor.
messages.activity-read-current-agent-sessions-and: Read current agent sessions and declared work in this project; Global aggregates authorized projects. Running/idle is separate from task blockers. Last-seen freshness is explicit. Follow next_cursor. Pass session_id only for your own exact native session to read its current-work revision and item keys. A permanent worker row also carries current_work {revision, item, item_key, updated_at, reviewed_at, stale}: its one shared assignment (revision 0 and no item until first written); authored text is visible to the team and unreadable Task details are withheld. For a worker that adopted Todo, current_work is projected from its board instead (source 'todo', plus focus and intent): the focused Task with its Intent, or no item when no focus is declared. Reads never acknowledge inbox events.
messages.activity-replace-or-explicitly-confirm-y: Replace or explicitly confirm your session’s current-work list (up to ten concurrent items), or patch selected items by item_key. Read agents_activity_list(session_id=your_native_session_id) for work_revision and item_keys. Patch actions add an item, replace an item by its current item_key, or remove it; unrelated and unreadable items remain untouched. Every write needs the exact current expected_work_revision. Empty items clears the list; empty patch confirms review. An unchanged update does not claim new progress. Write one short activity or blocker per item, aiming for about 50 characters (roughly 6–10 words) across summary and blocked_reason together; do not repeat the blocker. Keep IDs in reference fields and details in the linked Task or working memory. This is a writing target, not a validation limit; retain essential meaning. Update task outcomes separately; meaningful progress belongs in tasks_comment, not repeated waiting updates. A permanent worker has exactly one current assignment, shared with the team: zero or one item with a Task reference, a short description (summary plus blocked_reason; 100 words is the validation ceiling, not the writing target), or both. Once its Todo board is enrolled that focus is its assignment instead, and this operation returns an instruction to use todo_get and attention_focus_set; the stored record is kept for recovery and is no longer the assignment. It writes from its current native session (session_id); the installation owner or Ordubashy updates a worker with agent_id and no session_id. The first write expects revision 0 (the revision of an absent assignment); read current_work.revision and current_work.item_key (for a patch replace or remove) from agents_activity_list. Replacing the current Task needs replace_current=true; the previous Task is never completed for you, so record its state first.
messages.archive-ordubashy-propose-archiving-an-o: Ordubashy: propose archiving an owner project in Global. Always requires an urgent human Signoff, even with an allow override. Supply its current expected_revision. Approval hides the project from normal discovery and resets its terminal sessions. Keeps all records, folders, domains and mailboxes.
messages.archive-owner-list-archived-projects-tha: Owner: list archived projects that can be restored.
messages.archive-owner-restore-an-archived-projec: Owner: restore an archived project's resources to the active project menu. No agent is created, reactivated or prepared; historical agents stay inactive. Every active global agent reaches the restored project again through derived access.
messages.archive-project-to-archive-the-invocatio: Project to archive; the invocation and human review remain in Global.
messages.associated-read-the-actions-or-signoffs-: Read the Actions or Signoffs associated with a Task and, by default, with every Task below it in the same owning scope. Explicit ancestry, concerns relationships, an Action's task evidence, a Signoff's expected Task target and typed references on a Story Task's own discussion are the only associations; each record is read with its own permission, returned once by canonical identity and paged with a bound cursor. Withdrawn Actions and decided Signoffs remain part of the record's history. For the installation owner, a business-operational Action stored in Global is also associated when it is explicitly shared with the requested business and its bare task evidence names exactly one Task among Global and the Action's shared businesses, in that business; that inferred path is owner-only. A Task that was moved between scopes keeps the records established while it was in an earlier scope (audited stay and the record's own immutable revision or proposal time) and reads a discussion reference in the scope the message was written in; each such record is read with the caller's current authority in that scope and an unavailable one is omitted without a trace; a moved Task whose audited journey cannot be proven gains no inferred Action or Signoff (explicit relationships and typed references still apply).
messages.associations-existing-tasks-in-this-proj: Existing Tasks in this project to relate the new item to (each a group Task or any related Task).
messages.attention-action-for-the-founder-owner-o: Action for the founder/owner. One short, direct action in very simple words; omit filler and repeated context. Mark links as [short label](https://url). Use typed references for internal records. Do not write a separate recommendation.
messages.attention-curate-persistent-focus-presen: Curate persistent Focus presentation; source permissions and conversations remain independent.
messages.attention-detail-includes-full-tasks-sum: detail includes full Tasks; summary returns board rows; focus omits memberships.
messages.attention-focus-only-name-written-by-the: Focus-only name written by the curator. Use very simple words; aim for 2 words, at most 4 when possible. Leave out the project name because its tag is shown separately. Example: Landing page review. This is guidance, not a word-count limit. Empty restores the full source title.
messages.attention-true-when-this-item-currently-: True when this item currently blocks further work. Clear when the block is gone; presentation only, not task state.
messages.attention-true-when-this-needs-prompt-at: True when this needs prompt attention due to a real time constraint or impact. Keep separate from blocker and clear when no longer urgent.
messages.batches-exact-ordinary-mcp-arguments-eac: Exact ordinary MCP arguments. Each write needs its own stable idempotency_key; scope and response_detail belong here.
messages.batches-execute-1-20-fully-specified-exi: Execute 1–20 fully specified existing Qorqut calls in order in one MCP request. Use for multiple task creations or mixed operations; each keeps its own permissions, scope, approval and idempotency key. Not atomic: earlier successes remain on failure. Inspect every labeled result; retry unchanged writes with the same keys. No nested batches or result references. Stops starting new entries after 30 seconds; unfinished entries are explicit. Native parallel tool calls remain useful for independent reads already grouped by your client.
messages.batches-stop-on-error-pending-approval-o: Stop on error, pending approval or async acceptance. Continue only for independently justified entries; pending is not applied.
messages.batches-unique-result-label-within-this-: Unique result label within this request.
messages.broadcasts-accepted-for-existing-callers: Accepted for existing callers; it adds no per-business rows. The global agents are listed once in the selected scope.
messages.business-briefing-one-bounded-snapshot-o: One bounded snapshot of a project: the shared published Context's revision and most connected nodes, open and blocked tasks, parent-Task work groups, routines and failed jobs, what waits on the owner, work done in the last 14 days, agent activity, project note headlines and KPIs. Call it first when you start work on a project; Global agents pass business_id. Sections you cannot read are marked unavailable; each section names the tool for details. Read-only; it never acknowledges inbox events.
messages.business-progress-owner-daily-installati: Owner daily installation-local counts across authorized workspaces: task completions, every inbox delivery, each learning first accepted and each distinct completed action once on its occurrence day.
messages.business-progress-owner-read-all-time-re: Owner read: all-time recorded totals and daily installation-local series for distinct tasks first marked done, completed actions linked to this project (on their occurrence day) and approved signoffs. Missing dates are explicit, never guessed.
messages.compose-business-on-the-project-route-gl: business on the project route; global from the root route names the project.
messages.compose-one-existing-readable-item-keepi: One existing readable item, keeping its own scope: an Action keeps its canonical action_id.
messages.compose-owner-and-configured-ordubashy-a: Owner and configured Ordubashy: actual readable records of the chosen source scope, for choosing an explicit link target. Candidates are authorized one by one; a link grants no access.
messages.compose-owner-and-configured-ordubashy-e: Owner and configured Ordubashy: explicitly associate one currently readable item with this Project, without changing its owning scope or granting access. Linking an already owned item is a no-op.
messages.compose-owner-and-configured-ordubashy-o: Owner and configured Ordubashy: one authorized Project item plus the appropriate existing domain read of that record for in-pane presentation. This is not arbitrary table access.
Owner and configured Ordubashy: one existing Project's name, slug, actual summary, revision and archive state. Project cards take the real name; a custom Focus display name never applies.

Owner and configured Ordubashy: one Project's accessible records - its own work, signoffs, actions, documents, tables, automation and other records plus explicitly linked items in any scope. Owned and linked yield one row with both flags; denied candidates are omitted.
messages.compose-owner-and-configured-ordubashy-r: Owner and configured Ordubashy: remove exactly this explicit association with its current revision. An owned item, a Project, its records and its conversations are never changed.
messages.compose-the-actual-project-uuid-on-a-bus: The actual Project UUID; on a business route it must be the selected project.
messages.compose-the-chosen-source-scope-a-projec: The chosen source scope: a project UUID, or null for Global.
messages.conversations-separate-summary-of-the-ac: Separate summary of the accompanying full message. Use very simple, common words. Aim for 2–5 words and keep it within 10 when possible; longer is allowed. Keep the full message complete.
messages.costs-owner-view-global-usd-spend-by-sou: Owner view: Global USD spend by source (observed Context filing charges and background AI estimates), with a cumulative daily series.
messages.dashboard-summary-owner-project-counts-a: Owner project counts and fourteen daily installation-local activity totals.
messages.dev-tickets-owner-close-or-reopen-a-syst: Owner: close or reopen a System Dev report using its current revision.
messages.dev-tickets-owner-list-system-dev-report: Owner: list System Dev reports, open by default.
messages.dev-tickets-read-one-system-dev-report-a: Read one System Dev report and its follow-up/resolution history when authorized.
messages.diagnostics-diagnose-your-own-preparatio: Diagnose your own preparation, inbox notice state and retained applications. Remains usable when mandatory context is unavailable. Reports actual error codes and repair ownership; never grants preparation or replays work.
messages.diagnostics-read-exact-live-mcp-schemas-: Read exact live MCP schemas for 1–10 named tools, including mutation options and all required fields. Optionally inspect configuration schemas for exact published plugin pins before requesting a grant. No execution.
messages.direct-explicit-owner-instruction-in-the: Explicit owner instruction in the submitting agent’s Chat
messages.environment-list-effective-settings-vari: List effective Settings variable names, configured (nonempty) status and origin (global/business). No values are returned. Role-private bindings are visible only to allowed registered roles in their scope. Optional names checks specific bindings; origin:null means absent or unavailable to your role. Project overrides, including empty overrides, win over Global. Follow next_cursor. Configured does not prove credentials are valid or that a tool can use them. Pass variable names to supported operations such as backups.pull endpoint_env/token_env; the existing runtime resolves values. This tool does not grant script execution or secret access.
messages.environment-retrieve-one-settings-value-: Retrieve one Settings value by key, including private context or credentials, only when environment_get is explicitly granted. Role-private values also require your registered role; they are never inherited across scopes. Project scope reads only that project's own Settings, without Global inheritance; Global scope reads Global Settings. Missing returns found:false/value:null; empty returns found:true/value:''. Values enter model context and may be saved in transcripts. Retrieve only what the task needs; never repeat secrets in messages, logs or tasks. Retrieval does not authorize payments or other external actions.
messages.environment-write-set-one-settings-key-v: Set one Settings key/value in the selected project, including credentials. Preserves unrelated settings and existing private-role restrictions; never writes Global Settings. Pass the actual value directly; empty stores an empty project override. Reuse idempotency_key on retries. Returns a receipt (key names and file hash, never values). New terminal sessions load updated environment values; existing shells are not restarted.
messages.file-links-build-an-ordinary-link-the-ow: Build an ordinary link the owner can click to read a file in the Qorqut file viewer. Give exactly one of path or document_id. A path is the file's absolute path under this instance's operations root (best when you know it), or relative to that root with its first folder kept: projects/<slug>/hq/notes/report.md or agents/<agent>/scratch/report.md, never starting at the project slug. document_id is a registered document readable in your current scope (Global agents select a project with business_id as usual). Optional label; optional version (document_id only) links one saved version instead of the current file. Returns viewer_url (root-relative) and a ready Markdown link: paste the returned markdown into your reply unchanged and never build the URL by hand. For a path this only builds text: nothing is read, listed or verified, and the viewer checks the file when the owner opens it, so never claim the file exists because a link was built. Grants no file access; only the owner's viewer reads content. Read-only.
messages.focus-ask-the-owner-for-browser-input-on: Ask the owner for browser input on the identified app/tab, after finishing the current browser command. Pauses automation until owner Done. No URL or approval authority; describe the actual tab from your last browser observation.
messages.focus-clear-focus-and-explicitly-cancel-: Clear Focus and explicitly cancel pending browser input. Does not complete tasks, dismiss signoffs or approve actions.
messages.focus-replace-your-ordered-focus-cards-w: Replace your ordered Focus cards with current object references and why they matter. Keeps any pending browser input. Use your session inbox consumer_id and freshly read revision.
messages.incidents-owner-inspect-one-system-dev-i: Owner: inspect one System Dev incident and bounded evidence.
messages.incidents-owner-list-bounded-system-dev-: Owner: list bounded System Dev incident summaries.
messages.init-ask-for-owner-attention-on-the-pres: Ask for owner attention on the presented workspace with a short reason. Presentation state only; this does not create a Focus card, task or signoff.
messages.init-present-a-permitted-workspace-to-it: Present a permitted workspace to its renderer with its optional selection fields, item and status. Stores presentation state only; content edits always use the owning feature's operations.
messages.init-read-stored-workspace-presentation-: Read stored workspace presentation state. Agents read their own; the installation owner may read a selected agent's. This never reads workspace content.
messages.init-read-the-installed-workspace-types-: Read the installed workspace types with each type's supported roles, renderer and presentation actions. A small registry, not an arbitrary UI builder.
messages.init-select-what-is-shown-in-the-present: Select what is shown in the presented workspace. Stores presentation state only and changes no content.
messages.inputs-answer-an-eligible-management-rou: Answer an eligible management-routed input request as the configured Codex Ordubashy. This never approves or executes a protected action.
messages.inputs-ask-the-owner-a-question-or-reque: Ask the owner a question or request input. Use a stable request_key for the same outstanding question. Answers are read through signoffs_get/list; this never runs an action.
messages.inputs-set-notification-urgency-blocking: Set notification urgency/blocking for your pending signoff. Active global Ordubashy may also reprioritize other agents' accessible pending signoffs. This never approves, answers, or executes a signoff. Include a reason; urgent/blocking notifications repeat hourly.
messages.inputs-withdraw-your-pending-input-reque: Withdraw your pending input request while retaining its history.
messages.integration-inspect-a-scoped-background-: Inspect a scoped background job. The initiating agent and owner can read its full result; other agents receive status and error codes for coordination without private payloads.
messages.journal-when-the-owner-asks-list-visible: List visible journal titles and dates relevant to the owner’s work. Does not change review or filing state.
messages.journal-when-the-owner-asks-return-the-c: Read a relevant visible journal entry in full, including title, date, checklist state, revision and content hash.
messages.legacy-owner-and-configured-ordubashy-re: Owner and configured Ordubashy read of the owner's reminders in the selected project (or Global from the root route). Safe stored fields only; no delivery, update or cancel.
messages.legacy-short-alias-for-the-owner-s-own-o: Short alias for the owner's own one-off reminders; prefer the reminders_* tools, which also support recurrence and other recipients. When the owner asks to be reminded, schedule one concise reminder with text and at; list, update or cancel with reminder_id and revision. Only the owner and Ordubashy may use it.
messages.legacy-when-to-remind-the-owner-include-: When to remind the owner; include a timezone offset.
messages.local-time-optional-occurrence-in-the-in: Optional occurrence in the installation timezone returned by actions_config_get: YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH (24-hour). No minutes, seconds or offsets. Omit for now. A nonexistent DST hour is rejected; a repeated hour means its first occurrence.
messages.main-shared-qorqut-dashboard-and-http-mc: Shared Qorqut dashboard and HTTP MCP service
messages.mcp-presentation-compact-by-default-summ: Compact by default. Summary is a bounded operational view (Focus boards or selected cards, without conversations or decision evidence); full is canonical. Text renders compact as YAML, not inside batches.
messages.mcp-presentation-compact-identity-scope-: Compact identity/scope by default. response_detail=summary is readiness metadata only, not instructions. Before entering another project or when context_refresh_required, read response_detail=context without sections for complete mandatory rules. sections is a partial lookup, never a substitute for that read; tool_names checks named capabilities; full returns diagnostic detail.
messages.mcp-presentation-compact-index-by-defaul: Compact index by default. response_detail=summary is an explicit bounded operational view; response_detail=full returns the canonical payload.
messages.mcp-presentation-compact-index-omitted-f: Compact index: omitted fields are empty or default. response_detail=full returns the canonical payload.
messages.mcp-presentation-compact-receipt-index-b: Compact receipt/index by default; platform defaults may be omitted, while authored sections remain exact. Use full for the canonical payload; text renders the compact result as YAML (fewest tokens; not inside batches). On write retries reuse the same idempotency_key.
messages.mcp-presentation-compact-status-attentio: Compact status/attention index. signoffs_get reads full proposal/answer evidence before acting; response_detail=full retains decision notes for bulk feedback review without per-item reads.
messages.mcp-presentation-context-only-return-exa: context only: return exactly these '## ' sections of the mandatory rules, with a hash manifest of every omitted section. Omit for the full rendered bundle.
messages.mcp-presentation-decision-bindings-and-a: Decision bindings and approval evidence are complete; change previews keep diffs and changed fields only, and mark bounded values. response_detail=full returns raw before/after.
messages.mcp-presentation-identity-scope-by-defau: Identity/scope by default; summary is readiness metadata, not instructions. Context without sections returns complete mandatory rules without inventories or work briefing. Full returns diagnostic detail.
messages.mcp-presentation-multiple-names-return-a: Multiple names return availability/mode/description; name a single tool (or use response_detail=full) for its exact input schema.
messages.mcp-presentation-note-text-is-complete-o: Note text is complete; omitted per-note attribution and empty fields are defaults. response_detail=full returns the canonical payload.
messages.mcp-presentation-optional-exact-operatio: Optional exact operation names/aliases whose current availability and permission to include. Unknown names are explicit. Use with compact or context.
messages.mcp-presentation-returns-a-compact-focus: Returns a compact Focus receipt with revisions; focus_get reads the full pane, or request response_detail=full.
messages.mcp-presentation-returns-a-compact-task-: Returns a compact task index/receipt; tasks_get reads fields and recent notes; tasks_notes_list pages older notes.
messages.mcp-presentation-returns-a-delivery-rece: Returns a delivery receipt (message/thread/event IDs), not the sent text; agents_messages_list reads history, or request response_detail=full.
messages.mcp-presentation-returns-a-short-decisio: Returns a short decision/execution receipt; approval may only queue execution. signoffs_get reads evidence; response_detail=full with the same idempotency key reads the canonical receipt without repeating the decision.
messages.mcp-presentation-returns-row-ids-revisio: Returns row IDs/revisions, not echoed cells; tables_rows_list reads values, or request response_detail=full.
messages.mcp-presentation-returns-the-created-sig: Returns the created signoff's status index; signoffs_get reads the full question and choices, or request response_detail=full.
messages.mcp-reads-optional-revalidation-focus-bo: Optional revalidation (Focus board lists only). Send empty string for a read_state token; echo it only while that exact result remains in current context. Same caller/session/query/view only. Unchanged returns data.not_modified, not an empty result. Omit after compaction or missing evidence. Always rechecks permissions and data.
messages.media-operations-document-keeps-any-file: document keeps any file up to 50,000,000 bytes. photo accepts only a static JPEG or PNG up to 10,000,000 bytes, is never converted, and is never sent as a document instead.
messages.media-operations-optional-local-message-: Optional local message_id from telegram_history, in your own chat.
messages.media-operations-optional-plain-text-cap: Optional plain-text caption, at most 1024 characters. Omit it for a file without a caption.
messages.media-operations-reply-answers-the-owner: reply answers the owner; update reports progress.
messages.media-operations-send-one-file-or-photo-: Send one file or photo to the owner in your own Telegram chat; you cannot choose the chat. source is a file below exports/ or downloads/ of your own workspace ({type: workspace, path}) or a registered document you may read ({type: document, document_id, business_id: null for Global}). expected_sha256 is the lowercase SHA-256 of the exact bytes you expect to send; a different file is refused. send_as=document sends any file up to 50 MB; send_as=photo accepts only a static JPEG or PNG up to 10 MB and is never converted or sent as a document instead. purpose=reply answers the owner and update reports progress. The optional caption (plain text, at most 1024 characters) and reply_to (a local message_id from telegram_history in your own chat) are frozen with the request. The bytes are copied once into a private snapshot when you call this, and that snapshot is what is sent: later edits, moves or deletion of the source change nothing, and reusing an idempotency_key returns the same queued file without copying or sending it again. The result is the local message_id, its attachment (filename, send_as, size, sha256) and the delivery state (queued at return; read telegram_delivery_get for sent, failed, cancelled or uncertain, and never assume either outcome for uncertain). A Telegram file is owner-facing communication, not blanket authorization; use Signoffs for approvals.
messages.media-sources-exactly-one-file-source-a-: Exactly one file source. A workspace file is a relative path below your own workspace and only in exports/ or downloads/. A document is a registered document ID with its business_id (null for Global).
messages.media-sources-the-lowercase-hexadecimal-: The lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the exact file bytes you expect to send.
messages.messages-default-inbox-terminal-targeted: Default inbox. terminal targeted retired project Dev agents and is refused; use inbox.
messages.messages-find-active-agents-in-the-selec: Find active agents in the selected scope, or all authorized projects with all_businesses=true. Filter role_id (for example global-worker). Each row includes business_id for sends; IDs are authoritative.
messages.messages-read-your-sent-and-received-mes: Read your sent and received message history in this scope, optionally one thread or one current counterpart (counterpart_id from a message). Reading never acknowledges inbox events. The owner or current Ordubashy may use retirement_backlog=true in Global scope for the frozen read-only retirement handoff.
messages.messages-send-a-durable-internal-message: Send a durable internal message to a scoped agent. For a reply, supply reply_to; recipient is inferred. No agent may message Learning Applier; those roles can send outbound. Not a task assignment or permission grant.
messages.models-a-suggested-context-object-this-a: A suggested Context object this Action relates to. Pointers are suggestions, never required graph subjects.
messages.models-optional-typed-evidence-of-the-re: Optional typed evidence of the result (URL, commit, pull request or record IDs).
messages.moves-owner-and-configured-ordubashy-mov: Owner and configured Ordubashy: move the previewed Tasks and all descendants into the destination project in one transaction, keeping every Task id, internal parent, discussion, private conversation and link. Requires the preview token and an idempotency key; a changed state is revision_conflict (preview again) and an incompatible one is move_blocked.
messages.moves-owner-and-configured-ordubashy-rea: Owner and configured Ordubashy: read exactly what moving these Tasks and their descendants into the destination project would carry, the parent detachment of each root, the visibility consequence and every blocker. Writes nothing. The token binds the apply to this exact state.
messages.moves-owner-and-configured-ordubashy-the: Owner and configured Ordubashy: the active projects Tasks may be moved into from this source (a project UUID or null for Global), by name. Never truncated: more than 1000 is result_too_large.
messages.moves-root-tasks-to-move-with-all-of-the: Root Tasks to move with all of their descendants (1 to 100, at most 1000 in total).
messages.moves-the-active-destination-project-nev: The active destination project; never inferred.
messages.moves-the-project-the-tasks-are-in-now-i: The project the Tasks are in now: its UUID, or null for Global.
messages.notify-stable-identifier-of-the-conditio: Stable identifier of the condition; the same key updates one post.
messages.notify-what-happened-the-impact-and-the-: What happened, the impact and the action needed.
messages.notify-why-the-owner-must-know-now: Why the owner must know now.
messages.operational-delegation-manage-or-checkpo: Manage or checkpoint a durable bounded assignment.
messages.operations-add-a-comment-to-an-action-s-: Add a comment to an action's discussion (it changes neither the action nor its revisions, and queues nothing for Context). Needs its own permission and an active participant invoking in the action's owning namespace: being linked to an action is read access only. You follow the discussion by default unless you explicitly unfollowed it. The registered coordinator may relay an explicit installation-owner statement or another agent's report with relay; the recorder is always kept and a relay is never approval.
messages.operations-add-a-label-to-the-shared-tag: Add a label to the shared tag catalog (or find the existing one: labels equal by normalized text are one entry). Labels cannot be renamed or merged. Applying a tag to a Task or Action also creates it, so this is only needed to prepare a label in advance.
messages.operations-add-a-message-to-a-table-s-sh: Add a message to a table's shared discussion (ordinary and CRM tables alike). An archived table can still be discussed. The installation owner's team comments follow the same channel rule as Task discussions. Commenting needs the table's row-write permission as a policy decision only: it grants no data change.
messages.operations-add-an-entry-to-a-crm-table-w: Add an entry to a CRM table with the table's expected_revision: name exactly one of record (an existing Task of any type, by its scoped reference) or create (a new Customer, by default, made by tasks_create in the same atomic change). cells hold local values only; shared fields are edited on the Task with tasks_update. Adding a removed entry restores it with its data; adding an active one returns it unchanged unless different values conflict.
messages.operations-an-identity-id-from-fastmail-: An identity id from fastmail_identities_list; its email must equal from_address.
messages.operations-apply-the-terminal-outcome-of: Apply the terminal outcome of one registered Context filing (worker only; the receipt ID is the only input).
messages.operations-archive-a-note-while-preservi: Archive a note while preserving its contents and relationships. A project note also needs target_business_id.
messages.operations-archive-an-asset-while-preser: Archive an asset while preserving its bytes and relationships.
messages.operations-archive-or-restore-an-item-wi: Archive or restore an item without deleting its content or relationships. Does not cascade. Requires the item's expected_revision. Agent retirement and project membership use their dedicated administration tools.
messages.operations-ask-for-another-attempt-at-th: Ask for another attempt at the blocked head of this namespace. The driver starts the attempt; this records only the request.
messages.operations-browse-scoped-context-metadat: Browse scoped context metadata with pagination, without loading document bodies.
messages.operations-change-an-entry-s-local-cells: Change an entry's local cells (omitted keys are kept, null clears) and/or its stage (null clears) with the table's expected_revision. Shared Task fields are never written here. Name either entry_id with changes (one entry), or updates: a list of 1-100 {entry_id, changes} items, never both. To change several entries of the same table, send ONE call with updates instead of repeating this call or batching it: all rows share the one starting expected_revision, succeed or fail together, take one table revision and snapshot, and return a compact {table_id, table_revision, entries: [{entry_id, revision, changed}], job_id?} instead of each entry. Each entry may appear once. After a lost response retry the exact same whole request with the same idempotency_key.
messages.operations-children-of-this-parent-or-nu: Children of this parent, or null for top-level tasks.
messages.operations-classify-a-project-material-o: Classify a project Material or replace its descriptive tags, using expected_revision. Never edits its body, origin, relationships or permissions. Email stays conversation; raw uploads stay mixed. Personal/agent notes and plans use their own tools.
messages.operations-comments-per-page-newest-firs: Comments per page, newest first (0 omits them). Keep it unchanged when paging.
messages.operations-correct-an-action-you-recorde: Correct an Action you recorded (the installation owner and configured Ordubashy may correct any Action they can read): supply the fields to change (text, category, business_ids, real_time, tags, related_objects, evidence) with expected_revision. The correction is a new immutable revision queued for Context; earlier revisions are kept. Identity, origin, performer and recorder never change. A withdrawn Action cannot be corrected: record a new one.
messages.operations-create-a-directional-relation: Create a directional relationship. Prefer predefined roles; custom roles and duplicates are allowed. This never grants access or wakes an agent. Assign tasks using tasks_assign.
messages.operations-create-a-google-meet-link-on-: Create a Google Meet link on a Google event.
messages.operations-create-a-new-project-an-empty: Create a new Project: an empty container for Tasks, documents, tables, assets and code. Supply name (required, up to 200 characters), optionally summary (the project's Description, up to 2000 characters, may be empty) and optionally slug (the folder name under projects/: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter, up to 64 characters; when omitted it is derived from the name). A later name change never renames the folder. Creation makes only the project record, the owner's membership and an empty projects/<slug> folder with hq/ and code/: no agents, documents, Tasks, routines, Context inputs, external accounts or domains, and no session is started. If the folder name is taken the call fails with revision_conflict and the available suggested_slug; nothing existing is ever adopted. Only the configured Ordubashy can create projects; the owner and other agents ask Ordubashy. The response returns business (id, slug, name, summary, workspace_path, hq_path), business_id and slug. Retry the same idempotency_key after interruption.
messages.operations-create-or-update-a-masked-ema: Create or update a masked email, if the account advertises it.
messages.operations-create-your-private-note-with: Create your private note. With target_business_id (the selected project) it is a project note instead, written under the ordinary notes grant; tags label either kind.
messages.operations-defaults-to-not-currently-sno: Defaults to not currently snoozed. Snoozed tasks are the backlog. Closed/archived filters apply independently.
messages.operations-delete-one-message-the-delete: Delete one message. The delete itself is a provider action with no permanent-delete flag.
messages.operations-discard-this-namespace-s-bloc: Discard this namespace's blocked head, or an input that never started. A blocked input is discarded after the driver completes the mechanical Context discard.
messages.operations-do-the-action-on-the-screen-t: Do the action on the screen, then reply "done" to this message.
messages.operations-durable-workers-use-the-exact: Durable workers use the exact assignment target. Native helpers should omit this field; the server selects the parent configured browser.
messages.operations-edit-a-note-with-expected-rev: Edit a note with expected_revision. A project note also needs target_business_id equal to its project.
messages.operations-edit-a-relationship-s-endpoin: Edit a relationship's endpoints, role or explanation using its expected_revision. Workflow edges must use their domain tools.
messages.operations-edit-person-details-including: Edit Person details, including contact email/phone/notes and summary. document_id also accepts a human Person ID. Affiliation changes follow context_people_affiliation_set permissions.
messages.operations-establish-a-supported-global-: Establish a supported global agent with ecosystem scope. The owner creates ordubashy or learning-applier (at most one active each) or any number of global-worker agents; retired roles cannot be registered or switched to; name, display_name and assignment_brief are required. Ordubashy creates global workers only: name and assignment_brief suffice, role defaults to the newest published global-worker, display_name to the name, runtime to Ordubashy's, and scope to ecosystem with shared-context read access; no plugins are granted unless selected. Projects have no resident agents. Every global reaches every active project; a saved allowed_business_ids list is ignored. When plugins is omitted, only Ordubashy receives the published email-management guidance package and every other agent gets none; an explicit list, even empty, replaces the defaults. Ordubashy can grant a worker only core permissions and capabilities he holds himself and never administrative powers; published plugins are selected independently and keep their own permission checks.
messages.operations-exact-chat-id-from-whatsapp-r: Exact chat ID from whatsapp_read, never a contact name.
messages.operations-exact-owner-instruction-from-: Exact owner instruction from the current conversation authorizing this decision for this proposal. Not source evidence, a recommendation, or standing permission.
messages.operations-explicitly-retry-paused-globa: Explicitly retry paused Global transcript snapshots; normal routines leave this false.
messages.operations-find-directional-relationship: Find directional relationships by source, target, role or item. Returns authorized endpoint labels and explanations. No cross-business results.
messages.operations-find-existing-context-items-b: Find existing context items before linking them. Filter Materials by material_type, origin or tag. Raw uploads and archived items are excluded by default.
messages.operations-follow-or-unfollow-a-table-s-: Follow or unfollow a table's discussion for yourself. Creators and commenters follow by default; an explicit unfollow stays until you follow again. Following a table never follows its entries' Tasks.
messages.operations-follow-or-unfollow-a-task-s-d: Follow or unfollow a task's discussion for yourself. Creators, assignees and commenters follow by default; an explicit unfollow stays until you follow again. Required responsibility updates still reach responsible assignees.
messages.operations-follow-or-unfollow-an-action-: Follow or unfollow an action for yourself. The recorder follows by default; an explicit unfollow stays until you follow again. Followers are told when it is corrected or withdrawn.
messages.operations-forward-one-message-with-its-: Forward one message, with its original body and attachments, from a real account identity.
messages.operations-historical-binding-of-an-emai: Historical binding of an Email Task, kept read-only. Ordinary writes omit it; changing the type away from email clears it.
messages.operations-iana-timezone-e-g-america-new: IANA timezone, e.g. America/New_York. Required for timed recurring events.
messages.operations-icalendar-rrule-exdate-rdate-: iCalendar RRULE/EXDATE/RDATE lines; [] removes recurrence. Series edits use the master event ID.
messages.operations-inline-attachment-data-is-lim: Inline attachment data is limited to 1 MiB base64 across the whole request.
messages.operations-iso-date-for-all-day-events-o: ISO date for all-day events, or ISO date-time with UTC offset.
messages.operations-learning-applier-and-owner-on: Learning Applier and owner only. Create, update or delete one open Context review question outside the published Context; this never edits the graph or notes. Review manually: read the questions, preview and propose a supervised context_edit, get the owner's approval, apply it, and delete only the questions the owner's answers resolved. When an answer is unknown leave the question unchanged. Results carry question IDs and links only; read a question with context_questions.

Learning Applier and owner only. List open Context review questions kept outside the published Context (action=list, optionally filtered by one related_kind and related_id, with offset and limit) or read one (action=get, question_id). Each question has its ID, text, origin event and the linked event, node, edge or note IDs. An empty list is not proof that no review is needed. Start a review only when the owner asks.
messages.operations-learning-applier-only-record-: Learning Applier only: record the owner's explicit accept/reject instruction for one open learning. Requires current expected_revision and idempotency_key. The instruction is agent-reported, not independently authenticated. Never decide autonomously.
messages.operations-legacy-callers-only-omit-when: Legacy callers only; omit when using handle.
messages.operations-list-authorized-completed-act: List authorized completed actions by occurrence (newest first) with their recorded local date, category, business, performer and tag filters; withdrawn actions are omitted unless requested. With a project selected you see the actions linked to that project; without one, agents holding read_global_context see global-operational and their accessible business-operational actions.
messages.operations-list-preferred-relationship-r: List preferred relationship roles. Custom snake_case names are allowed when no predefined role fits. Workflow roles use their dedicated tools.
messages.operations-list-the-bundled-icons-a-work: List the bundled icons a worker can be given as presentation.icon, as {icons: [{id, label}]}. Choose an ID from this list; presentation replaces the whole object, so repeat any color to keep it.
messages.operations-list-the-shared-tag-catalog-e: List the shared tag catalog: every label ever used on a Task or Action, in the form it was first created. Tags are labels only: they grant no access and the catalog shows no item contents or counts.
messages.operations-list-this-namespace-s-context: List this namespace's Context inputs in queue order, with their states. queue_blocked tells whether the shared queue is stopped on a blocked input (which delays every later input); the blocked input is named only when it belongs to this namespace.
messages.operations-list-your-own-notes-with-targ: List your own notes. With target_business_id (the selected project), list that project's notes instead; tag keeps only notes carrying that tag.
messages.operations-literal-word-and-prefix-searc: Literal word and prefix search over published node and edge summaries and attributes, note text and committed source text, filtered by kind (node, edge, note or source) or attribute values. Notes are separate records, not graph nodes. Empty query browses. Follow page.next_cursor as cursor with the same arguments; results stay at the revision of the first page. An empty result is not proof of absence.
messages.operations-look-up-a-mutation-by-its-req: Look up a mutation by its request id (the job id returned when it was queued): the engine's receipt, if it holds one, and the job's own state, which is also how a mutation that has not reached the engine yet (queued, retrying or unconfirmed) is observed.
messages.operations-maintained-current-summary-an: Maintained current summary and next steps; history stays in the Task discussion and related items.
messages.operations-manage-tasks-in-the-selected-: Manage tasks in the selected project, or use scope=global for Global-only work. Global tasks are not inherited by projects; only the owner and granted global agents have access.
messages.operations-mark-move-trash-or-restore-on: Mark, move, trash or restore one message (ordinary organizing).
messages.operations-one-published-node-relationsh: One published node, relationship (edge), note or source by its reference (node:ID, edge:ID, note:ID, source:ID or a bare five-character ID): its summary, attributes, relationships, committed evidence and change history; a note's exact text and the nodes and relationships it links, each labeled current or removed; or a source's committed text. Follow the history and text next_cursor values to keep reading the same revision. A source reference never opens the protected operational source.
messages.operations-one-shared-deferral-of-the-ta: One shared deferral of the Task's due reminder, as a timezone-aware future timestamp; null clears it. It is not a state, a due date or a subscription change.
messages.operations-optional-rationale-of-the-rec: Optional rationale of the recording agent. It is stored separately and never as the owner's reasoning.
messages.operations-optional-record-the-result-of: Optional: record the result of your own COMPLETED delegated assignment. The server verifies that you own the assignment, that it completed with a recorded result and that the projects are within its scope; the performer is then unknown, you are the recorder and the assignment is kept as provenance. Each assignment's result is recorded once, and not at all when its worker already recorded its actions.
messages.operations-optional-uuid-of-your-own-cho: Optional UUID of your own choosing, given on acquire (or a handle-less command) to keep separate tasks apart; omit it for the default. Any UUID works and none is looked up or verified. Later calls use the returned handle.
messages.operations-ordubashy-only-on-acquire-wit: Ordubashy only, on acquire with protocol=handles: the id from action=list of the exact browser to control. Omit for your own configured browser (the default). The returned handle is bound to that browser; later calls cannot change it.
messages.operations-owner-only-queue-the-removal-: Owner only. Queue the removal of the exact published source of an upload from the shared Context. A pending input is discarded with its own control instead; this is not a rollback of other graph changes.
messages.operations-owner-status-of-the-telegram-: Owner status of the Telegram bridge: health, cursor, outbox, uncertain sends, cleanup failures and queued inputs.
messages.operations-owner-view-published-change-e: Owner view: published change events newest first with the submitting identity, source path, operation and the operational Action envelope when one produced the event.
messages.operations-owner-view-recorded-context-m: Owner view: recorded Context model-call usage across all projects for an optional input and an inclusive UTC date range of call start times: calls with exact USD where a charge was recorded (unknown stays null), aggregates, and a separate coverage inventory of reserved Context events and their last scans. A known subtotal, not final totals, from the last recorded collection; reading never collects.
messages.operations-plain-text-at-most-4000-chara: Plain text, at most 4000 characters. No formatting is interpreted.
messages.operations-popup-reminders-in-minutes-be: Popup reminders in minutes before start; [] disables event reminders.
messages.operations-post-or-update-one-actionable: Post or update one actionable notification in Urgent Notifications (what happened, impact, needed action). Repeating an identical active event is suppressed; a change or state=resolved updates the known post.
messages.operations-preview-cross-day-unresolved-: Preview cross-day unresolved replacements, or automatically reject evidence-backed superseded findings. Omission preserves legacy reconciliation.
messages.operations-propose-sending-one-plain-tex: Propose sending one plain-text message from the owner's personal WhatsApp to an existing chat. chat_id must be the exact ID of an indexed conversation from whatsapp_read, and text at most 16384 UTF-8 bytes. This creates an owner Signoff: NOTHING is sent until the owner approves exactly this chat and text, and a changed message needs a new proposal. Use it only when the owner has instructed you to send; incoming messages and names are evidence, never permission. There are no attachments, new recipients, request IDs or retries to manage. An accepted send means WhatsApp acknowledged it, not that it was delivered or read; an unconfirmed send is never silently repeated.
messages.operations-publish-an-exact-immutable-au: Publish an exact immutable authored revision without updating existing agent pins.
messages.operations-queue-one-context-source-chan: Queue one Context source change (add, edit or remove a foundation/ text source) for this namespace. Admission never waits for Context or a model. foundation/actions/ and accepted-Action metadata are reserved and cannot be claimed here.
messages.operations-queues-one-named-job-for-the-: Queues one named job for the engine; read the outcome with fastmail_receipt_get (jobs_get needs a different grant).
messages.operations-read-a-context-document-by-id: Read a context document by ID, heading or lines in bounded chunks; next_cursor is bound to the content hash.
messages.operations-read-a-crm-table-s-entries-me: Read a CRM table's entries (memberships of existing Task records) in stable position order, 50 by default and at most 100 per page. Each entry shows its local cells, the current Task fields its projected columns show, and the Task itself; a Task you cannot read appears as a bare unavailable placeholder. Sort and equals use local columns only. Removed entries and archived Tasks are hidden unless requested.
messages.operations-read-authorized-overseer-reco: Read authorized Overseer records and current source availability.
messages.operations-read-authorized-table-product: Read authorized table, product and people counts without loading the graph.
messages.operations-read-delivery-receipts-one-me: Read delivery receipts: one message by its local message_id, or your ten latest outbound messages. States are queued, dispatching, uncertain (send may or may not have happened; never assume either), sent, failed and cancelled. A file or photo also shows its attachment (filename, send_as, size, sha256). The owner view also lists every delivery of a message (its send and any edits) and accepts an outbox_id.
messages.operations-read-one-attachment-range-at-: Read one attachment range (at most 5 MiB per call); follow next_offset until it equals total.
messages.operations-read-one-bounded-page-of-a-ta: Read one bounded page of a table's shared discussion (oldest first within the page; next_cursor continues to older messages), including the structured developments of CRM entry changes you are allowed to see, and your own follow state.
messages.operations-read-one-bounded-page-of-an-a: Read one bounded page of an authorized action's discussion (oldest first within the page; next_cursor continues to older messages). Authorized exactly like actions_get: unauthorized or unknown actions are not found, and a project that can read a shared action reads its discussion. Reading never follows the action.
messages.operations-read-one-message-with-its-exp: Read one message with its expected_state. Optional account_id must name the configured account.
messages.operations-read-one-of-this-namespace-s-: Read one of this namespace's Context inputs with its immutable payload, attempts and control requests.
messages.operations-read-one-relationship-includi: Read one relationship, including direction, role, explanation and creation/update timestamps.
messages.operations-read-one-thread-page-at-most-: Read one thread page; at most 100 messages per page. Optional account_id must name the configured account.
messages.operations-read-only-inventory-of-retain: Read-only inventory of retained procedural (bucket delta) learning records for a later owner migration decision. This target writes none and proposes no conversion, import or deletion.
messages.operations-read-the-actual-owner-answer-: Read the actual owner answer to your exact proposal Signoff and update the shared delta queue. Response contains reference (provider, signoff_id, proposal_revision, payload_hash, status_revision) and interpretation (null for a choice without notes; otherwise clarity/action/rationale). Never applies active files.
messages.operations-read-the-last-messages-defaul: Read the last messages (default and maximum 10, oldest first) exchanged with the owner in your own Telegram chat since activation. Secret replies are redacted. A file or photo shows its attachment (filename, send_as, size, sha256); one without a caption shows File: or Photo: and its filename as text. Signoffs and other chats are never included.
messages.operations-read-the-owner-s-fastmail-acc: Read the owner's Fastmail account through the bounded engine API.
messages.operations-read-the-project-context-map-: Read the project context map, or one item's immediate neighborhood. Original uploads and generated projections are never map nodes. Reading does not acknowledge context.
messages.operations-read-your-current-identity-ro: Read your current identity, role, grants and project orientation. Select business_id only within your allowed scope. Reading never acknowledges context.
messages.operations-read-your-submitted-instructi: Read your submitted instruction, exact review Signoff and decision; performs no application.
messages.operations-record-an-email-message-or-de: Record an email, message or development you observed about a Task, with its source reference and the time it really happened. This is an append-only record attributed to you: it sends nothing, fetches nothing, verifies nothing and approves nothing. The same event_key returns the original; a correction is a new event naming the earlier one (corrects_event_id).
messages.operations-record-one-atomic-completed-r: Record one atomic COMPLETED result (not a task description, plan, proposal, status change or failed attempt) in the canonical action log. Text is the result in at most 20 words for agents; no task, title or time is required. Omitted real_time means now; supplied real_time uses the installation timezone from actions_config_get, YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH. Agents holding read_global_context record in Global: category is required (global-operational or business-operational); business-operational needs business_ids of currently authorized, active projects, and one inaccessible project rejects the whole call. An agent without read_global_context records only with a project selected: text only; the action is business-operational for that project. Tags come from the shared tag catalog (tags_list); a new label is created by using it, and a tag grants no access. related_objects are optional suggestions of Context objects the result concerns. Every accepted record is queued for Context as revision 1. You are the performer and recorder of your own work; never record another actor's work as yours or duplicate system receipts.  Ordubashy may record reported completed owner or agent work using performed_by and a matching explicit_owner_statement or agent_report relay. The authenticated caller remains recorder; owner_intent does not prove completion.
messages.operations-remove-an-entry-from-a-crm-ta: Remove an entry from a CRM table with the table's expected_revision. This is a soft removal of the membership only: the Task, its thread and its history are untouched and adding the Task again restores the entry.
messages.operations-remove-only-this-relationship: Remove only this relationship using its expected_revision. Items and their contents are preserved. Workflow edges must use their domain tools.
messages.operations-replace-one-draft-s-content-n: Replace one draft's content; nothing is sent.
messages.operations-reply-to-this-message-with-th: Reply to this message with the requested code. It is kept only briefly and typed to the agent; Telegram chats are not end-to-end encrypted.
messages.operations-reply-to-this-message-with-yo: Reply to this message with your answer.
messages.operations-resolve-a-context-item-to-its: Resolve a context item to its current title, subtype, archive state and domain resource identity.
messages.operations-resolve-one-uncertain-telegra: Resolve one uncertain Telegram send or edit, named by its exact outbox_id from status or telegram_delivery_get. mark_delivered records the exact Telegram message ID the owner saw (for an edit, the ID of the message that was edited); retry queues it again under its saved target and binding and can duplicate a send, and an edit that a newer update of its event already replaced is closed instead of sent. expected_revision is the receipt_revision from telegram_delivery_get or status; a changed receipt is refused. Never changes a Signoff decision.
messages.operations-retry-the-current-source-of-a: Retry the current source of an unfiled upload: queue it as a new version when it changed, retry a blocked Context input, or requeue a filing job that failed before its completion applied. A discarded filing or a cancelled job is never revived.
messages.operations-run-an-authorized-overseer-br: Run an authorized Overseer bridge operation with its exact saved binding.
messages.operations-save-a-draft-from-a-real-acco: Save a draft from a real account identity; nothing is sent.
messages.operations-search-context-with-bounded-e: Search context with bounded excerpts. Check complete and follow refresh_cursor before concluding absence.
messages.operations-search-messages-in-the-accoun: Search messages in the account; at most 100 per page.
messages.operations-send-a-new-message-from-a-rea: Send a new message from a real account identity. The request id makes a repeat idempotent.
messages.operations-send-a-plain-text-message-to-: Send a plain-text message to the owner in your own Telegram chat; you cannot choose the chat. purpose=reply answers the owner, update reports progress, blocking_input asks for something you cannot continue without and requires request_key, reason and input_mode (text, secret or screen_action; secret requests expire within 10 minutes, and no secret is ever returned to you in history). Reusing a pending request_key returns the existing request. The result is the local message_id and its truthful delivery state (queued at return; read telegram_delivery_get for sent or uncertain). A Telegram message is scoped owner input, not blanket authorization; use Signoffs for approvals and durable questions.
messages.operations-send-a-reply-to-one-message-f: Send a reply to one message from a real account identity.
messages.operations-sending-requires-owner-approv: Sending requires owner approval of the exact recipients, subject, body and attachments. Use this operation instead of a generic input request. Save edits only revises the proposal; Approve queues sending.
messages.operations-set-a-person-internal-externa: Set a Person internal/external classification using current role permissions and scope; this never grants access.
messages.operations-set-the-account-s-vacation-re: Set the account's vacation responder, if the account advertises it.
messages.operations-set-up-diagnose-repair-restar: Set up, diagnose, repair, restart or stop an active worker's own configured browser (Ordubashy only; no owner approval is needed for this routine maintenance). status changes nothing. ensure creates a dedicated headless managed browser when the worker has none, or starts a stopped owned one, and leaves a healthy browser alone. repair also restores a missing target file from saved ownership and restarts an owned browser that does not respond. restart and stop act only on the exact owned browser and are refused while a browser command is running. Profiles, logins and conversations are always preserved; nothing is ever deleted. Mutations need an idempotency_key and report ready only after a real CDP health check. A pre-existing browser without a registered service binding answers browser_management_unconfigured: that is an installation step, not a missing permission. This grants no authority to spend, submit forms or act as the owner.
messages.operations-short-browser-handle-returned: Short browser handle returned by acquire; use it for subsequent actions. Configured-browser handles never expire; a durable worker's handle lasts as long as its turn. Server retains lease credentials.
messages.operations-stable-action-identity-reused: Stable action identity, reused exactly for reconciliation; defaults to the command idempotency_key.
messages.operations-submit-an-explicit-owner-chat: Submit an explicit owner Chat instruction as a proposed delta with an owner-only review Signoff. Supply the exact full original message, proposed change, scope (description, project_ids, work_types, workflow_refs, conditions, exceptions), and catalog target references. Reuse request_key on retry. Creates no active edit; acceptance queues separate application.
messages.operations-tags-are-ordinary-labels-that: Tags are ordinary labels that group work; they never grant access or select an assignee. Preserve unrelated tags on updates. Tags come from the shared tag catalog (tags_list); a new label is created by using it.
messages.operations-task-for-an-actionable-step-s: task for an actionable step; story for an ongoing relationship, opportunity or work group; customer for a person or company; email for a historical Task bound to one email conversation (its binding is read-only).
messages.operations-the-account-s-folders-with-th: The account's folders with their ids and state.
messages.operations-the-account-s-sending-identit: The account's sending identities (id, name, email). An alias is an identity here.
messages.operations-the-active-permanent-worker-w: The active permanent worker whose own browser to administer.
messages.operations-the-configured-fastmail-accou: The configured Fastmail account: its id, supported actions, folders and identities.
messages.operations-the-exact-message-at-most-163: The exact message, at most 16384 UTF-8 bytes.
messages.operations-the-fastmail-account-id-repor: The Fastmail account id reported by fastmail_capabilities_get.
messages.operations-the-owner-s-own-explanation-f: The owner's own explanation for this decision, exactly as they gave it in the current conversation. Omit it when the owner gave none: never ask for one and never write your own here.
messages.operations-the-parent-task-in-the-same-o: The parent Task in the same owning scope (null for none). Parent and child states are independent.
messages.operations-the-relationships-around-a-pu: The relationships around a published node out to depth 3 (in, out or both), nearest first, as a bounded page pinned to one revision.
messages.operations-the-shared-published-context-: The shared published Context graph: a bounded page of node summaries and attributes with their relationships, most connected first. Every response names the published revision it was read at; follow page.next_cursor as cursor to keep reading that same revision. An initialized empty graph says empty; a status other than ready says why nothing could be read.
messages.operations-this-mutation-does-not-send-e: This mutation does not send email.
messages.operations-use-a-browser-over-trusted-mc: Use a browser over trusted MCP. Native callers use their own configured browser lease-free: acquire returns a handle at once, command runs immediately, and release is a no-op; nothing waits or needs reconciling. A timed-out command returns an error: inspect the page before repeating a state-changing action. Projects have no browsers. Durable workers use an exclusive turn on their assignment's configured browser; the handle needs renew, release, and reconcile of an uncertain action before retry. Acquire with protocol=handles, then use handle for command/release. Handle callers never pass lease IDs or tokens, and no browser endpoint is returned. Ordubashy alone may call action=list for the managed Global browsers (id, label) and acquire any of them by browser_id; listing or referencing a browser in chat takes no turn. Waiting releases execution capacity and never grants shell or arbitrary network access.
messages.operations-use-handles-on-acquire-for-co: Use handles on acquire for compact replies and server-held credentials. Default legacy preserves unrefreshed callers.
messages.operations-withdraw-an-action-you-record: Withdraw an Action you recorded (the installation owner and configured Ordubashy may withdraw any Action they can read) with expected_revision. The Action and its history stay readable, marked withdrawn; the withdrawal is queued for Context as a removal and the Action accepts no later change.
messages.operations-worker-only-output-of-the-sch: Worker-only output of the scheduled extraction program: record its one derived due occurrence.
messages.overview-ordubashy-only-brief-owner-self: Ordubashy only: brief owner/self task overview across Global and all currently authorized projects in one call, regardless of selected project. Defaults to both assignees, unfinished non-archived tasks, active and snoozed separated. Entries include revision and every tag label (or []); titles capped at 180 characters; no notes or custom fields. Counts cover all matches; follow next_cursor if present. Use the returned revision for optimistic edits to explicit overview fields such as due and tags. Read tasks_get first when editing fields or evidence not shown here.
messages.owner-actions-ordubashy-only-propose-eng: Ordubashy only: propose engineering_update in an authorized project. Supply expected_revision of the project config, parameters and rationale. Always stages an exact-change owner Signoff; never applies on chat consent or an allow override. No signoff approvals, credentials, shell commands or arbitrary owner actions.
messages.owner-bootstrap-a-specific-owner-instruc: A specific owner instruction (for example "create these tasks" or "complete this task") authorizes that Qorqut operation without a second confirmation; ask only for missing scope or a materially different action. Tool access alone never authorizes unrelated writes, and current revisions, idempotency keys, state transitions and excluded operations still apply.
messages.owner-bootstrap-deeper-context-is-fetche: Deeper context is fetched on demand: start with context_home, search context_find, then read context_object and context_expand. This orientation is an index, not the whole graph.
messages.owner-bootstrap-direct-coordination-uses: Direct coordination uses agents_message_recipients, agents_message_send and agents_messages_list within this project; create and assign same-business tasks when work needs durable follow-up. These messages are distinct from the owner_conversation private discussion attached to a task, Signoff or email object.
messages.owner-bootstrap-no-autonomous-work-loop-: No autonomous work loop is started and nothing is claimed, announced, handed off or reported automatically. Read a task or Signoff only when the owner's current request refers to it.
messages.owner-bootstrap-orientation-for-an-owner: Orientation for an owner-directed code session: the bound project, its coordinator, its engineering authority, registered repositories and code root, the shared published Context home, and a bounded index of further context. Returns no tasks, Signoffs or inbox data and changes nothing.
messages.owner-bootstrap-project-direction-belong: Project direction belongs to the owner with Ordubashy, who delegates bounded work to the permanent workers; the project's notes are listed with notes_list (target_business_id) and read with notes_get. Projects have no resident agents: Ordubashy coordinates execution across projects and the global agents work here when the owner directs them.
messages.private-conversations-list-readable-owne: List readable owner–Ordubashy threads by their last real message. Does not mark them read.
messages.private-conversations-read-related-recor: Read related records for visual thread context. Never creates conversation messages.
messages.private-conversations-read-the-private-o: Read the private owner–Ordubashy conversation on one object. It is the only private channel: agent_id and peer_role may only restate Ordubashy.
messages.private-conversations-record-the-owner-s: Record the owner’s private read position up to a sequence the server already returned.
messages.private-conversations-send-one-private-m: Send one private message to the owner–Ordubashy channel on this object. It never posts to the team discussion and never changes the source.
messages.private-conversations-show-the-owner-s-o: Show the owner’s one private channel on this object, Ordubashy’s, and its unread state. No other peer exists. Does not mark messages read.
messages.reads-owner-shared-content-history-of-on: Owner: shared content history of one document in the selected scope: one version, a diff between two versions, or a page of version metadata (no contents).
messages.reads-owner-the-selected-project-s-recor: Owner: the selected project's recorded activity facts, newest first, from the core source and its sequence cursor.
messages.rejection-ordubashy-only-reject-a-pendin: Ordubashy only: reject a pending action signoff with optional feedback using its freshly read binding. Cannot approve, retry, or answer input requests.
messages.review-byte-continuation-of-the-exact-se: Byte continuation of the exact selected page; repeat the same evidence_cursor/history_cursor arguments.
messages.review-continue-the-append-only-history-: Continue the append-only history collection at this position.
messages.review-continue-the-frozen-evidence-coll: Continue the frozen evidence collection at this position.
messages.review-read-one-retained-learning-candid: Read one retained learning candidate with its owner decision, reasoning and bounded frozen extraction cores (quoted evidence and source hashes, never original transcripts). Evidence and history are independent collections: follow next_evidence_cursor and next_history_cursor until both are null to enumerate the whole saved record, and merge the page_collections this page carries. Sources are keyed by both run and session; missing saved cores are explicit. An oversized page comes back in complete:false with next_content_cursor; reassemble it with the same collection arguments before following either collection cursor. Historical procedural records are read_only.
messages.review-read-the-compact-factual-context-: Read the compact factual Context review agenda across authorized scopes; defaults to open. Excludes filed and collapsed items. Does not approve anything and returns no issue projection.
messages.reviews-explicitly-incorporate-related-c: Explicitly incorporate related context or explain why no change is needed. Supply the item's expected_revision and observed relationship/source/review versions. Optional edit to this same item commits atomically under its normal domain policy. Never acknowledge context merely read or filed.
messages.reviews-read-shared-pending-context-or-i: Read shared pending context or immutable review decisions for this item. Reading does not acknowledge context. Each endpoint reviews related evidence independently of the other endpoint.
messages.reviews-reopen-this-item-s-shared-review: Reopen this item's shared review of a relationship, retaining every earlier decision. Requires current item, relationship, review-state and source versions and an explanation.
messages.schemas-characters-of-a-source-s-committ: Characters of a source's committed text per page.
messages.schemas-node-id-edge-id-note-id-source-i: node:ID, edge:ID, note:ID, source:ID or a bare five-character ID from a previous result.
messages.schemas-nodes-per-page-most-connected-fi: Nodes per page, most connected first.
messages.service-a-time-with-its-timezone-offset-: A time with its timezone offset, for example 2026-11-02T09:00:00-05:00.
messages.service-acknowledge-exact-handled-events: Acknowledge exact handled events; a read or a nudge never clears them.
messages.service-change-a-reminder-using-its-curr: Change a reminder using its current revision. A null recurrence makes it one-off and needs at. A time, recurrence or recipient change discards the pending delivery; a text or metadata edit does not.
messages.service-clear-the-current-due-occurrence: Clear the current due occurrence using its occurrence_id. A repeating reminder stays enabled. Reading or acknowledging a notice never dismisses it, and dismissing never completes a linked task.
messages.service-create-a-reminder-for-yourself-t: Create a reminder for yourself (the owner and Ordubashy may name another recipient_id). Give at for a one-off time, or recurrence {schedule, timezone} to repeat on the Routines calendar; one card is kept per repeating reminder and only the latest missed occurrence is delivered. linked_item must be readable by creator and recipient.
messages.service-defer-a-scheduled-or-due-reminde: Defer a scheduled or due reminder to a future time. Repeats before that time are suppressed, then the original calendar resumes.
messages.service-five-field-cron-minute-hour-day-: Five-field cron: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week.
messages.service-follow-an-authorized-item-a-task: Follow an authorized item. A Task, Action or Table follow is the same preference as tasks_follow/actions_follow/tables_follow and is removed the same way. Only a Task follow can include its directly related work (its child Tasks and the items it is linked to, one hop); that routing lasts while the Task is followed, with no recursive following or time expiry. Remove it with inbox_unsubscribe. The installation owner or Ordubashy may pass agent_id to follow for a global worker; the item must then be readable by that worker.
messages.service-iana-timezone-name-for-example-a: IANA timezone name, for example America/New_York.
messages.service-list-authorized-management-intak: List authorized management intake with source links and actual attribution.
messages.service-list-authorized-subscriptions-in: List authorized subscriptions, including automatic owner-task follows for Ordubashy. An ID identifies a removable manual follow; id=null means automatic-only. Removing a manual follow never disables automatic following. The installation owner or Ordubashy may pass agent_id to list a global worker's subscriptions, authorized as that worker.
messages.service-list-visible-proposals-in-the-se: List visible proposals in the selected project, or scope=global. Ownership fixes the review destination.
messages.service-list-your-reminders-scheduled-an: List your reminders (scheduled and due by default). The owner and Ordubashy may list another recipient_id or all_recipients; all_scopes spans projects and Global. Bounded pages with next_cursor.
messages.service-one-concise-sentence-the-recipie: One concise sentence the recipient will read when the reminder is due.
messages.service-read-a-batch-of-your-pending-upd: Read a batch of your pending updates. For a fresh reconciliation omit after (or use 0); use next_cursor as after only to continue that bounded pass. A notification watermark does not prove earlier events were handled. Reading never acknowledges. Your authenticated agent identity selects the inbox; consumer_id is accepted for older clients but is unnecessary.
messages.service-read-a-proposal-and-owner-feedba: Read a proposal and owner feedback in the selected project, or with explicit scope=global and global rights.
messages.service-read-one-authorized-management-i: Read one authorized management intake item.
messages.service-read-one-reminder-you-may-see-it: Read one reminder you may see: its state, next time, current occurrence_id and revision.
messages.service-remove-an-explicit-subscription-: Remove an explicit subscription by subscription_id, or a Task, Action or Table follow by source_type and source_id (the same preference as tasks_follow/actions_follow/tables_follow); automatic owner-task following is independent. The installation owner or Ordubashy may pass agent_id to remove a global worker's. Already delivered updates remain pending until acknowledged.
messages.service-resolve-or-dismiss-a-management-: Resolve or dismiss a management route while retaining its immutable canonical source.
messages.service-route-one-canonical-message-or-i: Route one canonical message or input request to management or owner attention.
messages.service-send-a-durable-management-messag: Send a durable management message to the exact configured coordinator.
messages.service-set-the-one-installation-managem: Set the one installation management coordinator. The target must be an active Ordubashy.
messages.service-stop-the-whole-reminder-or-serie: Stop the whole reminder or series and discard any pending delivery.
messages.settings-operations-patch-editable-setti: Patch editable settings in the selected project with current expected_revision. Nested objects merge; null removes a value. Unmentioned fields are preserved. Read business_config_get first.
messages.settings-operations-replace-editable-set: Replace editable settings in the selected project using the current expected_revision. Preserve unrelated config fields. The owner and scoped Ordubashy may directly manage engineering organizations/repositories/deployment targets; other agents cannot. Projects have no browser settings. Registered identity, owner and paths remain protected. Tool overrides still apply.
messages.source-operations-explicit-typed-edit-of: Explicit typed edit of the published Context, in two variants selected by the plan's format. (1) Queued graph edit: one qorqut-graph-edit-v1 plan (put_node, put_edge, remove_node, remove_edge with full records, your own five-character IDs, explanations, citations and support) against the current published revision. It is queued in the shared Context order and a later driver step publishes exactly that plan as one event with no model, if your authority and the base still hold. Result: the queued input and its execution facts; nothing is published when this returns.
